question.problem: Given that ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{{log}_{9}⁡x}{k},$ what is the value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
We use the change of base formula:

$$
{log}_{a}⁡X=\frac{{log}_{b}⁡X}{{log}_{b}⁡a}
$$

We want to change from base $a=3$ to base $b=9.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{3}⁡x & =\frac{{log}_{9}⁡x}{{log}_{9}⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Rewriting the expression in the denominator using exponents, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{log}_{9}⁡x}{{log}_{9}⁡3} & =\frac{{log}_{9}⁡x}{{log}_{9}⁡({9}^{1/2})} \\  & =\frac{{log}_{9}⁡x}{(\frac{1}{2})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{{log}_{9}⁡x}{(\frac{1}{2})}.
$$

Hence, $k=\frac{1}{2}.$
